paper.title: Language Generation with Infinite Contamination
paper.summary: Studies element and set generation when repetition-free presentations may contain finite, vanishing-rate, or constant-rate additive noise and may omit target elements. The Lean development covers the principal separations, priority algorithms, explicit-family Theorems 5.1, 5.4, 6.1, and 6.5, the arbitrary-constant Theorem 6.4 obstruction, and bounded-displacement density change, while recording the later infinite-noise and element-density theorems as open.

formalization_scope.summary: The formalization has complete semantic interfaces and complete explicit-enumeration paths through the central finite-contamination set-density characterization, but the later infinite-noise set-density, element-density, and bounded-displacement generation results remain open.
specializations: Theorems 5.1, 5.4, 6.1, and 6.5 are packaged for a collection supplied by an explicit countable enumeration.
The development is semantic and classical and does not establish computability or complexity bounds.
gaps: Theorems 6.11 and 6.14 and the element-density Theorems 6.15--6.18 are not formalized.
Algorithm 9 and Theorem 7.8 are not formalized.

claims.title: Contamination regimes and fresh element/set generation
claims.statement_summary: The paper defines repetition-free presentations with finite, vanishing, or constant-rate noise and several omission regimes, together with element and infinite-set generators whose late outputs are target-valid and fresh.

source_assessment.notes: The semantic interfaces are coherent; zero-length empirical noise is conventionally assigned rate zero.

claims.statement_summary: At every fixed priority cutoff, the selected finite class eventually stabilizes; when a selected prefix contains that class and has infinite common intersection, a fresh target point exists.

claims.title: Finite contamination transfers through finite language expansions
claims.statement_summary: A finite-noise, finite-omission presentation is an exact presentation of a finite expansion of the target, and eventual element or set generation for the expansion transfers back after finitely many extraneous values have appeared.

source_assessment.notes: The deterministic finite-expansion reduction is well specified.

formalization.notes: The expansion witness and all three transfer modes are proved; the complete source construction is not packaged.

claims.statement_summary: For an explicitly indexed countable family, Algorithm 4's priority ordering, maximal infinite prefix, and geometric thresholds define one generator that eventually emits fresh target elements under vanishing noise and arbitrary omissions.

source_assessment.notes: The printed proof reverses its final common-core containment; Lean proves and uses the corrected direction.

claims.title: Constant-noise generation is characterized by infinite stable finite intersections
claims.statement_summary: For an explicitly enumerated countable collection, element generation under constant noise and arbitrary omissions is equivalent to the source's finite-subcollection common-stream condition that forces an infinite common core.

source_assessment.notes: The implication formulation used in Lean is logically equivalent to the source's alternative.

formalization.notes: Both necessity and sufficiency are combined for the explicit enumeration interface.

claims.title: Compatible nested targets obstruct better set density
claims.statement_summary: If one stream is compatible with nested targets, validity for the smaller target bounds the achievable set density in the larger target; the paper instantiates this obstruction at arbitrary constants.

source_assessment.notes: The obstruction is semantic; lower mechanical words supply exact arbitrary densities, with the even numbers retained as the elementary one-half specialization.

formalization.notes: Lean proves the semantic obstruction, exact arbitrary-density mechanical-word witnesses, their canonical presentations, the uniform two-target impossibility theorem, and the one-half specialization.
